cases.case: Known Service ID answered with 200 and a schedule document
cases.what: A sid equal to a configured service's UniqueIdentifier, with a valid start and end, gets 200 with a TV-Anytime schedule document, valid against the TV-Anytime schema of the V1.2.1 attachments in the repository's XSD test (T1).

cases.case: Unknown Service ID answered with 200 and empty tables
cases.what: An unknown sid is answered 200 with an empty ProgramInformationTable and ProgramLocationTable, for timestamp and now/next requests alike.

cases.case: start and end filter the events returned
cases.what: Only events whose PublishedStartTime is at or after start and before end are returned; the generated schedule is the same for any window, so adjacent windows join up.

cases.case: 400 for a missing, invalid or misaligned start or end
cases.what: start and end are checked against every limit of the clause (whole numbers, multiples of 10 800, a span of 6 or 12 hours, no earlier than midnight at the start of today minus 28 days, no later than midnight at the end of today plus 28 days), and a request breaking any of them, or missing either, is answered 400.

noted: The optional inclusive parameter is ignored, which the clause allows ("if supported").
The schedule is generated by repeating the configured programme list back to back from the Unix epoch, so it does not reflect real broadcast times.

requirements.name: Now/next filtered schedule request (server)

cases.case: now_next=true on the ScheduleInfoEndpoint
cases.what: now_next=true on the schedule endpoint returns the on-air event as the only member of the now group and the next event as the only member of the later group, with no earlier events.

cases.case: now_next=window (up to ten earlier and ten later events)
cases.what: now_next=window returns the on-air event with up to ten earlier and up to ten later events.

cases.case: GroupInformationTable with the now, later and earlier structural groups
cases.what: The response has a GroupInformationTable with one GroupInformation per non-empty now, later and earlier group (ordered true, numOfItems, GroupType ProgramGroupTypeType with value otherCollection, empty BasicDescription), and each ProgramInformation has a MemberOf with the group CRID and its @index, counting forward in the later group and backward in the earlier group.

noted: A second now/next URL, not signalled in the list, is kept for direct callers and answers as now_next=true.

requirements.name: Schedule response

cases.case: Well-formed document with ProgramLocationTable and ProgramInformationTable
cases.what: Schedule and now/next responses with events are TV-Anytime documents with both tables, valid against the attached schema; a recognised service with no events for the request gets both tables, empty, which also validates.

cases.case: Every ScheduleEvent has a ProgramInformation, and only those
cases.what: A ProgramInformation is written for each event returned, with the CRID of its ScheduleEvent Program@crid, and none for anything else, in timestamp and now/next responses.

cases.case: Empty Schedule element for a recognised service with no events
cases.what: A recognised service with no programmes, or none starting in the requested window, is answered 200 with an empty TV-Anytime document that holds no Schedule and neither table; the empty Schedule element the clause asks for would fail the attached TV-Anytime schema.
cases.conflict: TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 6.5.4.1: "If there are no matching schedule events for a requested service and the service is recognized by a Content Guide Server, then an empty Schedule element shall be returned for the service." (table 50, clause 6.10.6, row ScheduleEvent, agrees: "Optional {0..n}"). Against: tva_metadata_3-1.xsd (TS 103 770 V1.2.1 annex B attachment), complexType ScheduleType (line 901), line 903: "<element name="ScheduleEvent" type="tva:ScheduleEventType" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>"; with no minOccurs the default of 1 applies, so every Schedule needs at least one ScheduleEvent and an empty Schedule element is invalid.

cases.case: OnDemandProgram returned for events also available on demand
cases.what: Each returned event whose programme has a catch-up URL also gets an OnDemandProgram in the ProgramLocationTable with the same Program@crid; publishing a catch-up URL without a usable catch-up player is refused.

cases.case: Schedule@serviceIDRef matches the service identifier of the request
cases.what: Schedule@serviceIDRef echoes the sid of the request, which is the service UniqueIdentifier.

cases.case: Schedule@start and Schedule@end
cases.what: @start is the start of the earliest event returned and @end the end of the latest, both in UTC with the Z designator, as table 50 defines them.

noted: The timestamp schedule response also carries a GroupInformationTable of series groups; clause 6.5.4.1 lists that table for now/next and window responses, and says that when it is present the order of programmes is given by structural CRIDs.
Each occurrence of a programme gets its own CRID naming the service and its start, so no @programId repeats within a response.
A configuration file edited outside the server with a catch-up URL but no usable catch-up player is served without OnDemandProgram for those programmes, with a warning in the log.

requirements.name: Programme information request (server)

cases.case: Request by pid answered with one extended ProgramInformation
cases.what: A request by pid returns one ProgramInformation, the same as in schedule responses, and a ProgramLocationTable holding the programme's OnDemandProgram when it is on demand and empty otherwise.

cases.case: Unknown CRID answered with 200 and empty tables
cases.what: An unknown, malformed or absent pid is answered 200 with an empty ProgramInformationTable and ProgramLocationTable.

noted: The programme response carries the same data as the schedule and nothing beyond it; clause 6.6.3 lets extended information be added if available.

requirements.name: Metadata profile of guide responses

cases.case: TVAMain@xml:lang
cases.what: Every guide response sets @xml:lang on TVAMain to the list's language.

cases.case: ProgramInformation@programId and BasicDescription
cases.what: Each ProgramInformation has a crid:// @programId and a BasicDescription.

cases.case: Title with @type main
cases.what: One Title with type="main" is written from the configured programme title.

cases.case: Title at most 80 characters
cases.what: Publishing refuses a programme title longer than 80 characters (counted in Unicode code points), so no longer title is written.

cases.case: Synopsis with @length medium
cases.what: One Synopsis with length="medium" is written per programme, and publishing refuses a description longer than 250 characters, the medium limit.

cases.case: ParentalGuidance with mpeg7:MinimumAge
cases.what: When a programme has an age rating, one ParentalGuidance with mpeg7:MinimumAge is written.

cases.case: Programme image: one RelatedMaterial, image/jpeg or image/png
cases.what: At most one RelatedMaterial is written for a programme image, with @contentType, and only when the image is image/jpeg or image/png, a data: image only when its bytes are that format; other images are not signalled.

cases.case: MemberOf@xsi:type MemberOfType
cases.what: Every MemberOf, for series and for the now/next groups, carries xsi:type="MemberOfType".

cases.case: ScheduleEvent Program, PublishedStartTime and PublishedDuration
cases.what: Each ScheduleEvent has Program@crid, PublishedStartTime in UTC with Z and an ISO 8601 PublishedDuration.

cases.case: OnDemandProgram@serviceIDRef
cases.what: OnDemandProgram carries @serviceIDRef: the sid of the request, or the service's UniqueIdentifier in a programme request, which has no sid.

cases.case: OnDemandProgram ProgramURL is an XML AIT with @contentType application/vnd.dvb.ait+xml
cases.what: ProgramURL carries @contentType application/vnd.dvb.ait+xml and points at the provider's content deep-linked XML AIT for the programme, served with that media type, whose URLBase and applicationLocation launch the operator's configured catch-up player at the programme; the XML AIT validates against the XML AIT schema in the repository's test (T1).

cases.case: OnDemandProgram InstanceDescription with two availability Genre elements
cases.what: InstanceDescription holds two Genre elements with @type other: MediaAvailabilityCS media_available while the programme is inside its availability window (else media_unavailable), and FEPGAvailabilityCS fepg_unavailable, the default.

cases.case: OnDemandProgram PublishedDuration, StartOfAvailability, EndOfAvailability, DeliveryMode and Free
cases.what: All five are written: availability starts at the broadcast start and ends 30 days after the broadcast end, DeliveryMode is streaming and Free is true.

noted: Events that have started also carry ActualStartTime and ActualEndTime equal to the published values; the profile lists ActualStartTime and ActualDuration, not ActualEndTime, which a client may ignore.

No AuxiliaryURL (Template XML AIT) is written. Table 52 marks it "Optional {0..1}", while clause 5.2.4.4.2 reads "Within every OnDemandProgram element supplied through the content guide interface there shall be an AuxiliaryURL referencing a Template XML AIT." Writing one would satisfy both, so leaving it out does not meet clause 5.2.4.4.2; that clause is outside this requirement's locators and has no case here.
A programme without a description is written with an empty medium Synopsis.

The XML AIT endpoint accepts the regionID[] and lloc parameters the client appends without tailoring on them, and never returns the application/vnd.dvbi.non form clause 5.2.4.2 describes for content the provider cannot offer to a device.

requirements.name: Classification terms in guide responses

spec.locator: clause 6.10.5.2, table 42, row Genre; clause 6.11.5; clause 6.10.13, table 59, row HowRelated; clause 6.11.9, table 72

cases.case: Genre @type main
cases.what: Programme Genre is written with @href and a Name child and no @type, so the schema default of main applies, as the table requires.

cases.case: Programme Genre terms from ContentCS
cases.what: Programme genres are written as terms of urn:tva:metadata:cs:ContentCS:2011, a scheme clause 6.11.5 names; whether each term exists in that scheme is not verified, because ETSI TS 102 822-3-1, which defines it, is not held at a known version (reference [7] is undated and the scheme is not among the TS 103 770 V1.2.1 attachments).

cases.case: Programme image HowRelated term
cases.what: Programme images use urn:tva:metadata:cs:HowRelatedCS:2012:19 (Promotional Still Image), the term table 72 lists; table 59 requires a clause D.1 term for a programme image, and clause D.1 defines none, so no value meets both.
cases.conflict: TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 6.10.13, table 59, row HowRelated: "The @href attribute shall carry a value specified in clause D.1 where the RelatedMaterial fragment contains a link to an application, an application logo, service logo or programme image in the MediaLocator.MediaUri element." Clause D.1 (urn:dvb:metadata:cs:HowRelatedCS:2021) has terms only for service, service list and content guide material. Against: TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 6.11.9: "The values identified in table 72 are profiled from TV-Anytime, ETSI TS 102 822-3-1 [7]." Table 72 lists urn:tva:metadata:cs:HowRelatedCS:2012:19 (Promotional Still Image) for .../BasicDescription/RelatedMaterial/HowRelated[@href], and the example column of table 59 uses the same term for a programme image.
cases.locator: clause 6.10.13, table 59, row HowRelated; clause 6.11.9, table 72

noted: All eight ContentCS terms used were found in a TV-Anytime ContentCS file held locally whose specification version is not stated in the file; that is not a check against a known version.
No Restart, Box Set, More Episodes or audio terms are emitted, as the related features are not implemented.

spec.locator: clause 6.1; clause 5.5.2, Service table rows ContentGuideSource and ContentGuideSourceRef

cases.case: ScheduleInfoEndpoint URI read from ContentGuideSource
cases.what: For each ContentGuideSource, in ContentGuideSourceList, at list level or in a Service, the ScheduleInfoEndpoint URI is read with the ProgramInfo, GroupInfo and MoreEpisodes endpoints; list entries are kept by @CGSID.

cases.case: Service-level ContentGuideSource takes precedence
cases.what: A service's own ContentGuideSource is used first, before any reference or the list-level source.

cases.case: ContentGuideSourceRef resolved to a CGSID
cases.what: ContentGuideSourceRef is read and looked up among the ContentGuideSourceList entries by @CGSID; ContentGuideServiceRef is no longer used for this and only sets the guide service identifier.

cases.case: List-level ContentGuideSource for services with no source of their own
cases.what: A service with neither its own source nor a matching reference uses the ContentGuideSource element directly under ServiceList, or has no guide when there is none.

requirements.name: Guide request URL format (client)

cases.case: <api_endpoint_URL>[?<query_params>]
cases.what: Query parameters are added to the query of the endpoint URL from the service list with ? or &, before any fragment, before any proxy wrapping.

cases.case: Reserved characters in query values percent-encoded
cases.what: Keys and values are percent-encoded for every reserved character of RFC 3986 clause 2.2, the gen-delims : / ? # [ ] @ and the sub-delims ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =, with uppercase hexadecimal digits; square brackets in regionID[] and sid[] are sent as %5B%5D, and a service identifier such as tag:example,2026:svc is sent encoded.

noted: The serviceId parameter that TS 103 770 does not define is no longer sent; image_variant and inclusive, which the clauses make optional, are not sent either.
Pagination links are used as given, with only white space removed from the MediaUri text (clause 6.9 example URIs are wrapped across lines).
The character set of annex C of ETSI TS 102 809 that the clause also requires of query parameters is not judged here.

requirements.name: HTTP caching and error handling for guide requests (client)

spec.locator: clauses 6.2.3 and 6.2.4, referring to clauses 4.3.2 and 4.3.3 (the published text of 6.2.3 reads "4.3.24.3.2"); clause 6.5.1

cases.case: Cache-Control max-age honoured
cases.what: Guide requests go through the same HTTP client as service lists: a response's max-age is honoured per URL, so the five-minute refresh is answered from the local copy until it expires; request URLs are now stable (3-hour aligned schedule windows, fixed now/next URLs), and the proxy passes Cache-Control on.

cases.case: If-Modified-Since on repeated requests
cases.what: The Last-Modified time of each guide response is kept and sent as If-Modified-Since on the next request for the same URL.

cases.case: 400 or 406: request not retried
cases.what: A guide request answered with 400 or 406 is never sent again in the session; the next request differs only when a new 3-hour window starts, and the parameters now meet clause 6.5.2.1.

cases.case: 404 on a ContentGuideSource URL: re-acquire the service list, then back off
cases.what: A 404 from any guide endpoint of the ContentGuideSource (schedule and now/next, ProgramInfo, GroupInfo for box sets, MoreEpisodes) makes the client re-acquire the service list once, and a 404 again on the same request after that applies the back-off.

cases.case: 5xx or connection failure: retries no faster than the back-off model
cases.what: After a 5xx or a connection failure no guide request for that URL is sent before the clause 4.3.3.7 back-off wait has passed; the five-minute refresh is skipped until then.

cases.case: Single sid parameter
cases.what: Each schedule request carries exactly one sid.

cases.case: sid is ContentGuideServiceRef when present, else UniqueIdentifier
cases.what: sid is the service's ContentGuideServiceRef when it has one, else its UniqueIdentifier.

cases.case: start and end are whole multiples of 10 800 seconds
cases.what: start is rounded down to a 3-hour boundary, so it is a whole multiple of 10 800, and each further window starts 12 hours later.

cases.case: end is start plus 21 600 or 43 200 seconds
cases.what: Each request spans 43 200 seconds (12 hours); the period shown is covered by several requests whose results are combined.

cases.case: Times within 28 days back and forward
cases.what: The requested windows run from up to four hours before the current time to at most a day after it, inside the 28 day limits.

cases.case: Only services listed in a DVB-I service list
cases.what: Guide requests are made only for services parsed from the loaded service list.

cases.case: now_next=true on the ScheduleInfoEndpoint, without start and end
cases.what: The channel list is filled from <ScheduleInfoEndpoint>?sid=...&now_next=true, without start and end.

cases.case: now_next=window
cases.what: The selected service is queried with now_next=window, without start and end.

cases.case: Order of now/next events from the structural group CRIDs
cases.what: MemberOf of the now, later and earlier structural groups is read from ProgramInformation; when present, events are ordered by it (earlier counting back, later forward) and the event in the now group is taken as current.

requirements.name: Schedule response handling (client)

cases.case: Robust to element order and additional elements
cases.what: Elements are looked up by namespace and name wherever they appear, and unknown elements are ignored.

cases.case: ProgramInformation linked to ScheduleEvent and OnDemandProgram by CRID
cases.what: Programme details are keyed by ProgramInformation@programId and joined to ScheduleEvent and OnDemandProgram through Program@crid.

cases.case: Events re-ordered for the UI (should)
cases.what: Events are sorted for display, by the structural groups of a now/next answer or else by start time, as clause 6.5.4.2 says a client should do since events are not necessarily in order.

noted: Events with the same start time are reduced to one, and the start time shown is ActualStartTime when present; table 51 describes PublishedStartTime as the time displayed to the viewer.
The client handles only IP services, so the hybrid broadcast merging rules of clause 6.5.4.2 do not apply to it.

cases.case: Request <ProgramInfoEndpoint>?pid=<CRID>
cases.what: When an event is selected, the client requests <ProgramInfoEndpoint>?pid=<CRID>, the CRID being the event's Program@crid from the ScheduleInfo answer, and shows the long synopsis from the ProgramInformation returned.

requirements.name: More Episodes, Box Sets and pagination (client)

cases.case: More Episodes requests and display
cases.what: From the detail pane the client requests <MoreEpisodesEndpoint>?pid=...&type=ondemand with the region chosen in settings, shows the results in MemberOf@index order and hides those whose on-demand entry is unavailable or incompatible.

cases.case: Box Set Categories, Lists and Contents
cases.what: A toolbar button requests Box Set Categories, then Box Set Lists for a category and Box Set Contents for a box set, with the URL formats of clauses 6.8.2.2, 6.8.3.2 and 6.8.4.2 (paginated format).

cases.case: Pagination links and page handling
cases.what: Pages of any size are handled; the next page is requested from the pagination link as given, on request, or at once only when a page leaves nothing to show; GroupInformation@numOfItems is not displayed.

noted: Box sets whose Template XML AIT offers no application this client can start, and box set contents whose on-demand entry is unavailable or incompatible, are hidden. Clause 6.8.3.2 says the client "shall not filter the results, whether by region ID or other means", while clause 6.8.3.3 expects @numOfItems to differ from the items visible to the user due to content compatibility signalled in the Template XML AIT, and clause 5.2.4.4.1 says incompatible content shall be marked as unavailable. Not judged as a separate case.

requirements.name: Use of guide metadata (client)

cases.case: Programme ParentalGuidance enforced at playback
cases.what: Every ParentalGuidance MinimumAge with its CountryCodes is read; the programme on air is checked when a live service is selected and again when the guide's current programme changes, and an on-demand programme before it starts; a programme over the threshold is blocked, or asks for the PIN where one is set.

cases.case: OnDemandProgram ProgramURL used as an XML AIT to launch the player
cases.what: An on-demand item is offered only when its ProgramURL is an XML AIT; it is started by fetching that XML AIT, choosing its HTML5 application of a platform profile the client launches, and launching it in the player area.

cases.case: RelatedMaterial not referring to an image ignored
cases.what: Only RelatedMaterial with HowRelated term 19 (or the older 1001) is used as the programme image, and of it only a MediaUri signalled as image/jpeg or image/png; other RelatedMaterial is ignored.

cases.case: Robust to additional Genre elements
cases.what: The first Genre is used (its Name, or the last part of @href) and any further Genre elements are ignored without error.

noted: Watch again is offered for an ended event only when its OnDemandProgram is within StartOfAvailability and EndOfAvailability and its Template XML AIT has an HTML5 application; the media availability Genre is not read.
Audio, video and access-service attributes in guide metadata are not read, so the media metadata precedence of clause 6.12 has nothing to apply to.

The programme image term the client accepts (TV-Anytime HowRelatedCS:2012:19) is the one table 72 and clause 5.2.8.2.1 use; table 59 asks for a clause D.1 value, and D.1 has none for a programme image (SPEC-NOTES contradiction 10). The case above is judged on the table 42 sentence only.
The rating check at a programme change and before on-demand playback has no automated test of its own; only the check at selection is tested.

requirements.name: Content guide acquisition (Exo DVB-I Player)

cases.case: Content guide source discovery and guide requests
cases.what: The wrapper makes no content guide requests; any guide shown comes from the external DVB-I frontend it loads, which is not part of this repository.

cases.case: Guide presentation and on-demand launch
cases.what: The wrapper has no guide user interface; it only hands stream URLs requested by the frontend to ExoPlayer.

requirements.exists: An Android WebView loads a third-party DVB-I frontend from a fixed URL and passes any request for a .mpd, .m3u8, .mp4 or .ts URL to ExoPlayer.

features.name: TS 102 796 (HbbTV, via TS 103 770)
features.summary: TS 103 770 hands eleven obligations to TS 102 796 V1.8.1 (its undated reference [21], whose latest issue applies). The browser and Android clients follow the HTTP/1.1 caching rules it leads to (no-store, freshness from Age and Date) and make conditional requests; where RFC 7234 has a no-cache response validated and TS 103 770 forbids a request before max-age has passed, the specification is inconsistent, and the two clients took opposite sides. Both use the clause 11.2 TLS profile for metadata connections, except that Android still lets a TLS 1.2 server sign with SHA-1, and both launch linked applications with the clause 6.2.2.6.2 launch location and XML AIT applications only of a platform profile table 5 admits. The provider and registry serve with that TLS profile and ECDHE preferred; the provider writes the XML AIT of its catch-up player to table 7, warns but still publishes an http: URLBase, accepts versions other than the 1.8.1 table 5 sets, and signals only JPEG and PNG images whose bytes it checks where it holds them. Whether the trust stores match the HbbTV root certificate list is not judged. The Exo DVB-I Player makes no conditional request and keeps no cache, and makes no TLS connection; the DSM-CC carousel and the AppInformation URNs of annex H apply to no component (no broadcast tuner, no access service signalled through a linked application).

requirements.name: O1 HTTP caching rules and HTTP cache

cases.case: C1.1a A no-store response is not stored
cases.what: A response carrying no-store is not kept, and a copy already held for that address is dropped, also when a 304 answer carries it.

cases.case: C1.1b A stored response is reused only while fresh, its age taken from Age and Date
cases.what: A stored response answers a repeated request without contacting the server only while its max-age exceeds its age, counted from the Age and Date headers, which the proxy passes back; a response with no max-age, or more than one, is validated with a conditional request instead.

cases.case: C1.1c no-cache together with max-age
cases.what: A response with no-cache and max-age is answered from the local copy until max-age has passed, as TS 103 770 asks; RFC 7234 has it validated before every reuse. A no-cache response without max-age is validated on every request.
cases.conflict: IETF RFC 7234 clause 5.2.2.2: "The "no-cache" response directive indicates that the response MUST NOT be used to satisfy a subsequent request without successful validation on the origin server." against TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1: "If the max-age header is present, the DVB-I client shall only request updates after the duration signalled in the header has passed." RFC 7234 is reached through TS 102 796 V1.8.1 clause 7.3.2.6 and RFC 7230 clause 2.4.
cases.locator: IETF RFC 7234 clause 5.2.2.2; TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1

cases.case: C1.2 If-Modified-Since where the server gave Last-Modified
cases.what: The Last-Modified time held for a document is sent as If-Modified-Since on the next request for it, and left out when none is held; the proxy forwards it upstream.

cases.case: C1.3 If-None-Match where the server gave an ETag
cases.what: The ETag held for a document is sent as If-None-Match on the next request for it, and left out when none is held; a new ETag on a 304 replaces it; the proxy forwards the header upstream and the ETag back.

cases.case: C1.4 An HTTP cache for the content the client accesses
cases.what: One in-memory cache serves every request to a DVB-I endpoint (service lists, the registry, the content guide, XML AITs); images are loaded by the browser through its own HTTP cache.

noted: Reached through TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1: "The DVB-I client shall follow the cache control requirements in clause 7.3.2.6 of ETSI TS 102 796 [21]." Reference [21] is undated; V1.8.1 is its latest issue. Its reference [6] is IETF RFC 7230, whose clause 2.4 reads "HTTP requirements for cache behavior and cacheable responses are defined in Section 2 of [RFC7234].", so the caching rules are read in RFC 7234, of the same series.

Which status codes may be stored without explicit freshness (RFC 7234 clause 3, "a status code that is defined as cacheable by default", listed in RFC 7231 clause 6.1) and how Vary selects a stored response (RFC 7234 clause 4.1, Vary defined in RFC 7231 clause 7.1.4) are not judged: RFC 7231 is not held.

A 304 answer without Cache-Control leaves the stored response stale, so the next request for it is validated again; RFC 7234 clause 4.3.4 keeps the stored header fields a 304 does not replace. Validating sooner is always allowed, so no case fails on it.

Expires is not used as a freshness lifetime: a response with Expires and no max-age is validated before reuse, which RFC 7234 permits; Expires still sets when a Template XML AIT result is refreshed (TS 103 770 clause 5.2.4.4.5).

requirements.name: O1 HTTP caching rules and HTTP cache

cases.case: C1.1a A no-store response is not stored
cases.what: A response carrying no-store is not kept and a copy already held for that address is dropped, also when a 304 answer carries it.

cases.case: C1.1b A stored response is reused only while fresh, its age taken from Age and Date
cases.what: A stored response answers a repeated request without contacting the server only while its freshness lifetime, max-age or else Expires minus Date, exceeds its age counted from the Age and Date headers; a repeated max-age, or no lifetime, means the response is validated instead. A 304 replaces the stored header fields it carries before freshness is worked out again.

cases.case: C1.1c no-cache together with max-age
cases.what: A response with no-cache is validated with a conditional request every time, as RFC 7234 asks, even when it carries max-age, so a request is sent before max-age has passed, which TS 103 770 forbids.
cases.conflict: IETF RFC 7234 clause 5.2.2.2: "The "no-cache" response directive indicates that the response MUST NOT be used to satisfy a subsequent request without successful validation on the origin server." against TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1: "If the max-age header is present, the DVB-I client shall only request updates after the duration signalled in the header has passed." RFC 7234 is reached through TS 102 796 V1.8.1 clause 7.3.2.6 and RFC 7230 clause 2.4.
cases.locator: IETF RFC 7234 clause 5.2.2.2; TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1

cases.case: C1.2 If-Modified-Since where the server gave Last-Modified
cases.what: The Last-Modified time held for a document is sent as If-Modified-Since on the next request for it, and left out when none is held.

cases.case: C1.3 If-None-Match where the server gave an ETag
cases.what: The ETag held for a document is sent as If-None-Match on the next request for it, and left out when none is held; a new ETag on a 304 replaces it.

cases.case: C1.4 An HTTP cache for the content the client accesses
cases.what: An in-memory cache serves every request to a DVB-I endpoint; logos and programme images are loaded by the image library, whose own caching was not checked.

noted: Reached through TS 103 770 V1.2.1 clause 4.3.2.1: "The DVB-I client shall follow the cache control requirements in clause 7.3.2.6 of ETSI TS 102 796 [21]." Reference [21] is undated; V1.8.1 is its latest issue. Its reference [6] is IETF RFC 7230, whose clause 2.4 reads "HTTP requirements for cache behavior and cacheable responses are defined in Section 2 of [RFC7234].", so the caching rules are read in RFC 7234, of the same series.

Which status codes may be stored without explicit freshness (RFC 7234 clause 3, "a status code that is defined as cacheable by default", listed in RFC 7231 clause 6.1) and how Vary selects a stored response (RFC 7234 clause 4.1, Vary defined in RFC 7231 clause 7.1.4) are not judged: RFC 7231 is not held.

Any 2xx answer without no-store is stored; whether that is allowed for a status not cacheable by default needs RFC 7231 (see the note above). Such a response with no lifetime is never reused without validation.

requirements.name: O1 HTTP caching rules and HTTP cache

cases.case: C1.2 If-Modified-Since where the server gave Last-Modified
cases.what: The wrapper makes its own request for the service list, a plain GET at every start, and keeps no Last-Modified time, so the request is never conditional; the same finding as 4.3-exo.

cases.case: C1.3 If-None-Match where the server gave an ETag
cases.what: The same plain GET keeps no ETag, so no request carries If-None-Match.
